title: Detection Engineer
description:
Detection Engineer.
You think like an attacker and build like a defender. At DEFION, you transform real Red Team findings into detection rules that actually catch threats in production.
Where offense meets defense
DEFION has been protecting organizations since 2005. Our Detection Engineering team sits at the intersection of offense and defense: you take findings from real attacker simulations and Red Team exercises and translate them into detection rules that work across SIEM, EDR, and XDR platforms.
You will not just consume threat intelligence; you will generate it and apply it. You work in a multidisciplinary team alongside Red Teamers, Blue Teamers, and threat hunters in our Barcelona office (or remotely).
What you will do
Design, develop, and fine-tune detection rules in SIEM, EDR, and XDR platforms (Sentinel, CrowdStrike, Cortex, Splunk, and more)
Analyze results from attacker simulations to identify weaknesses in security controls
Develop detection and mitigation strategies for emerging threats using MITRE ATT&CK
Automate and optimize processes with Python, PowerShell, and Bash scripts
What you bring
Must have:
1-2 years of experience as Detection Engineer or SOC Analyst creating/optimizing alerts in SIEM/EDR
Knowledge of KQL (Kusto Query Language) and/or CQL (CrowdStrike Query Language)
Deep knowledge of Windows logs, telemetry, and event analysis for proactive threat detection
Strong understanding of adversary TTPs based on MITRE ATT&CK
Scripting skills in Bash, Python, or PowerShell
Knowledge of Windows and Linux system administration, TCP/IP, DHCP, DNS
Purple-team mindset: think like an adversary, enhance defensive capabilities
Clear communication in English for international team collaboration
Nice to have:
Cybersecurity certifications or a master's degree in a related field
Degree in Engineering, Cybersecurity, or related field
Why you will love working here
Red + Blue collaboration
Work closely with Red Team and Blue Team. Access to EDR, SIEMs, threat intelligence, and more.
Continuous training
Internal and external training, certifications, and annual conference attendance.
Career plan
A personalized professional development plan tailored to your interests and growth goals.
Barcelona office or remote
Flexible remote work or a comfortable office in central Barcelona. Summer reduced hours.
Health + benefits
Private health insurance, flexible compensation (meals, transport, childcare, training).
International team
Young, dynamic, and international team with an excellent work environment and work-life balance.

title: Planning & Support Coordinator

You make sure DEFION’s preventive services run smoothly. You keep track of planning, calendars and capacity, and flag in good time when something threatens to go wrong.
The linchpin of planning in Prevent
DEFION helps organisations become resilient against digital threats. Our Prevent department proactively reduces our clients’ attack surface: from vulnerability management and security awareness to pentests and risk assessments.
As Planning & Support Coordinator you support the Prevent managers in the day-to-day organisation of these services. You keep track of the planning of projects and recurring services, such as vulnerability assessments, pentests and awareness programmes, and make sure appointments, calendars and capacity line up. You are an important point of contact for consultants and clients on practical matters, and you flag early when something threatens to go wrong, so the managers can adjust quickly.

title: Senior Security Specialist Red Team
description:
Senior Security Specialist Red Team.
You have already run real red team operations and want to take the next step. At DEFION you join a red team that already carries out operations for clients. You help build it further and grow into the technical lead of the unit.
A red team that is already up and running, and that you will build out
Our Red Team already carries out red team engagements for clients: realistic attack simulations that show organisations how their prevention, detection and response hold up against a targeted attacker. The team stands on the shoulders of a large offensive security team with years of experience in complex infrastructure, cloud and Active Directory environments. You also work closely with colleagues in incident response and managed detection and response, who see every day how real attackers operate.
We want the Red Team to grow, in size and in capability. For that we are looking for a senior who already has red team experience and wants to set its technical direction.
What you will do
Red team operations
You carry out red team engagements and adversary simulations, from reconnaissance and initial access to lateral movement, persistence and achieving the objectives.
You design attack scenarios based on relevant threat actors and their TTPs, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.
You attack Active Directory, Entra ID and hybrid cloud environments and find your way past modern detection solutions.
You translate attack paths into clear reports for both the SOC and the client’s management, and facilitate purple team sessions.
Between operations you apply your expertise to assume breach, AD and cloud assessments.
Building out the Red Team
Together with the team you develop the red team proposition: which services we offer, to which clients and how we deliver them.
You sharpen the methodology, scenarios, reporting format and OPSEC guidelines.
You help build tooling, C2 infrastructure and evasion capability.
You are the technical sparring partner for sales and clients when scoping red team engagements.
Technical leadership
You take technical ownership of operations and safeguard the quality of the work.
You help recruit new team members and mentor pentesters who want to move into red teaming.
You are a sparring partner for colleagues on complex assignments and technical decisions.
Growing into tech lead
You start as a Senior Security Specialist in the Red Team and take technical responsibility for engagements from day one. As the team grows, you grow into its technical lead, responsible for the technical direction, the quality of the work and the development of the people. In your development plan we agree together what that step looks like and what you need to get there.
What you bring
Must have:
Several years of experience in offensive security, with a solid grounding in infrastructure, AD and cloud testing
Demonstrable experience with red team engagements, adversary simulation or assume breach assignments
In-depth knowledge of Active Directory, Entra ID and cloud environments (Azure and AWS)
Hands-on experience with at least one C2 framework, such as Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Mythic or Havoc
An understanding of how EDR and other detection mechanisms work and how attackers evade them
You can programme or script, for example in Python, C#, Go or PowerShell
A technical degree at university of applied sciences or university level, or a demonstrably equivalent level
Strong communication skills: you can explain an attack story clearly to engineers and management alike
You like to take the initiative, enjoy building things and want to make others technically better
Nice to have:
Experience leading a red team operation
Experience building your own tooling, implants or EDR evasion
Experience with threat intelligence-led red teaming under TIBER-EU or DORA TLPT
Offensive certifications such as OSEP, CRTO, CRTL or OSCE3
Published CVEs, your own tools or security research
